newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sets date for Latam's biggest sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sets date for Latam's biggest sell-off.

text.p: Brazil on Wednesday set a base price for mining colossus Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) that should guarantee it some $5.0 billion in receipts and make the sale Latin America's largest privatisation to date.

After months of dithering and delay caused by political and technical problems, Brazil's National Privatisation Council agreed a minimum price per share of 26.67 reais, giving CVRD a total value of 10.4 billion reais ($9.96 billion).

April 29 was the date fixed for the sale of an initial 45 percent of voting shares, which will form a Special Purpose Company to act as a holding for the mining conglomerate. The rest of Brasilia's 51 percent stake in CVRD's capital will be offered later to staff and floated in Brazil and overseas.
"All the technical details have been solved, all the problems resolved," Planning Minister Antonio Kandir said.
CVRD, set up 55 years ago, has evolved into the world's largest iron ore exporter and a major producer of most metals.
